title: Chiral $p$-Wave Superconductivity Proximate to a Fractional Chern Insulator and a Topological Charge Density Wave in a Moiré Chern Band
abstract: We study a spin-polarized moiré Chern band of twisted MoTe$_2$ with short-range repulsion, finding superconductivity proximate to a fractional Chern insulator at filling $ν=2/3$ and a topological charge density wave at $ν=3/4$. Exact diagonalization reveals pair binding over $0.7\lesssimν\lesssim0.77$, consistent with experiment, along with finite superfluid stiffness, chiral $p$-wave pairing correlations, and adiabatic connectivity to an attractive model. At weak repulsion, Kohn-Luttinger theory supports a Fermi-surface instability with the same pairing symmetry. The superconducting state has a Bogoliubov-de Gennes Chern number $C_{\mathrm{BdG}}=-1$, opposite to the normal-state Chern number at $ν=1$. Our results reveal interplay among superconductivity, fractional topology, and charge order.
summary: This work theoretically examines how superconductivity emerges in a moiré Chern band system, showing it exists near both a Fractional Chern Insulator and a Topological Charge Density Wave. Using ED and KL theory, the authors confirm chiral p-wave pairing and characterize the resulting superconducting state as topologically non-trivial ($C_{\text{BdG}}=-1$). This highlights the rich competition between different correlated electronic orders.
main_problem: The study investigates the complex interplay between superconductivity, fractional topological states (FCI), and charge order (TCDW) in a moiré Chern band system.
main_result: The system exhibits chiral p-wave superconductivity proximate to an FCI at $\nu=2/3$ and a TCDW at $\nu=3/4$, characterized by a topological superconducting state with $C_{\text{BdG}}=-1$.
method: The research employs Exact Diagonalization (ED) on finite clusters and utilizes Kohn-Luttinger theory to analyze pairing instabilities.
model_or_system: The physical system is a spin-polarized moiré Chern band derived from twisted $\text{MoTe}_2$, modeled with a continuum Hamiltonian and subjected to short-range repulsive interactions.
key_observables: Pair binding energy ($E_b$), superfluid stiffness, Bogoliubov-de Gennes Chern number ($C_{\text{BdG}}$), and pairing correlation functions.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system can be projected onto the lowest-energy band and relies on mean-field approximations (like KL theory) for certain analyses.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate pair binding across system sizes, the evolution of the ED spectrum, momentum distribution, and superfluid stiffness across different pairing regimes.
paper_structure: The paper analyzes the system by first establishing the model Hamiltonian, then using ED to find pair-binding signatures, and finally applying KL theory and topological invariants to characterize the resulting superconducting and ordered phases.
why_interesting: The interplay between topological order (FCI/Chern bands) and unconventional superconductivity is a major frontier in condensed matter physics, highly relevant to understanding emergent quantum phenomena in moiré heterostructures.
